newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries slightly firmer to steady in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries slightly firmer to steady in Tokyo.

text.p: Shorter-end U.S. Treasuries were slightly bid by Tokyo midday on Thursday due to light bargain hunting, but prices were generally moving in tight ranges.
"The underlying trend improved slightly after (Tuesday's) CPI data, but the consensus that the Fed may tighten credit in May remains strong," an U.S. brokerage trader said.
The firmness in shorter-end Treasuries provided an overall firm tone, which also pushed up T-bond futures.
Traders said more operators were willing to buy on dips, but Japanese institutional investors were keeping purchases small as the dollar trend remained bullish against the yen.

"Although the dollar has fallen back to around 125.50 yen, Japanese investors are still cautious," the trader said. "We know the investors have shown strong interest in buying Treasuries, but they seem to be reluctant now."
In New York on Wednesday, prices rallied late in the day to close with only modest losses after falling more than half a point early in the session when renewed rate hike fears grew.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond eased to 94-3/32, yielding 7.10 percent, from 94-5/32 in New York on Wednesday.
The June T-bond futures stood at 107-19/32, up 4/32 from the previous close.
